findings.F1: Among down days in folds B and C, the move after the day depends mostly on how wide the day was. Down days in each coin's widest high-low range quintile were followed by a next-day return +1.02 % above the coin's normal drift (t 4.36, 1003 cases). The four narrower quintiles gave between -0.16 % and +0.25 % (all t under 1.2).
findings.F2: The tested close-near-low effect is only present on wide days. Among down days in the top close-near-low quintile, the next-day excess return was +1.12 % (t 2.97, 223 cases) and +1.38 % (t 3.42, 239 cases) in the two widest range quintiles. In the three narrowest it was between -0.77 % and +0.05 % (all t under 1.9 in absolute value).
findings.F3: The effect also sits in high-volatility periods. With volatility measured as each coin's 20-day swing, down days closing nearest the low were followed by +1.79 % (t 4.85, 266 cases) in the top volatility tercile, against +0.08 % (t 0.28) and -0.12 % (t -0.34) in the middle and bottom terciles. The book's gain per bar in a position follows the same order: 0.49 % (t 5.55), 0.28 %, 0.12 % from high to low volatility.
findings.F4: The size of the fall grades the rebound with no close-location measure at all. The largest-fall decile of day returns was followed by +0.98 % above the coin's drift (t 4.12, 867 cases) and the second decile by +0.40 % (t 2.12). From the fourth decile up, the next day was flat to negative (-0.42 % to +0.05 %).
findings.F5: The mirror holds for wide up days. Up days in the widest range quintile were followed by -0.80 % against the coin's drift (t -2.97, 740 cases), and the fourth quintile by -0.43 % (t -2.05). The narrowest quintile gave +0.04 % (t 0.28).
findings.F6: The tested idea's per-case unusual move, +0.19 % (t 1.70), only equals the 0.19 % trade cost. The wide-range and high-volatility down days of F1 to F3 carry 1.0 % to 1.8 % per case, five to nine times that cost.
findings.F7: The effect is uneven over time, so it needs the held-out folds:

ideas.idea: After a down day, a coin rises over the next day, more so the further the day's close sits below its high, measured as a share of the close, so that a wide day closing at its low is followed by the largest rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader buys a down day's close in proportion to how far price fell from the day's high, and leaves small, narrow down days alone because their rebound does not cover the cost of a trade.
ideas.name: wide down-day drop from high

ideas.idea: In an agitated market, after a down day, a coin rises over the next day, more so the nearer that day's close sits to its low, as a share of the day's high-low range.
ideas.consequence: The low-close rebound is worth trading when the coin's 30-day swing is above its usual level, and not when the market is calm.
ideas.name: agitated low-close rebound

ideas.idea: After an up day, a coin falls over the next day, more so the wider that day's high-low range was as a share of its close.
ideas.consequence: A wide up day is a reason to cut or fade a long over the next day rather than to chase it.
ideas.name: wide up-day next-day reversal
